steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: A perspective or viewpoint is the writer's attitude, opinion or stance on a subject. It's what they think or feel about the topic they're writing about. | Word Connotations: The feelings and associations words evoke "Stubborn" vs "determined" - same behaviour, different attitude | Emotive Language: Words designed to provoke emotional responses "Murder" vs "killing" vs "death" - different emotional weights | Bias: A tendency to favour one side or perspective, often unfairly.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: What is the difference between perspective and bias? | Name three language features that might reveal a writer's perspective. | How can word connotations show perspective?
